Implications and equivalences for a morphism of schemes, based on Görtz and Wedhorn’s Appendix D.

Appendix DConnected diagramEquivalencesAll relations

The source calls universally injective morphisms purely inseparable. Radicial means universally injective. The labels ft, fp and lfp mean finite type, finite presentation and locally of finite presentation. The labels qc and qcqs mean quasi-compact and quasi-compact quasi-separated, respectively. Dashed arrows require the indicated hypothesis. Heavier arrows are the implications singled out in Appendix D. Select a node or arrow to read its Stacks references.         Bounded distributive lattice

        Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

        A lattice with least and greatest elements and distributive finite meets and joins. Its ideal completion is a coherent frame. Its prime spectrum carries the basic opens consisting of prime ideals missing a given element.

A sheaf FF satisfies F(U)≅Hom⁡(S,F)F(U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(S,F) by restriction for each S∈J(U)S\in J(U).

                                            H topology

                                            Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

                                            Generated by Zariski open covers and proper surjections on the finite-type site. Equivalently, use finite families whose coproduct is a universal topological epimorphism.

                                            Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.

                                            Local objects. For a separated Noetherian base S and an affine structural map P → S, the local lifting condition holds exactly for spectra of absolutely integrally closed valuation rings.

                                                Integral

                                                Hoyois diagrams · Absolute · global

                                                A scheme is integral when it is nonempty and every nonempty affine open has an integral domain as its coordinate ring. Equivalently it is reduced and irreducible.

                                                                      Plus construction over covering families

                                                                                          Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

                                                                                          The site uses admissible open subspaces and admissible coverings. On affinoids the admissible cover condition is tested using finite affinoid refinements; arbitrary unions of point sets do not supply the cover condition.

                                                                                            Rigid analytic pro-étale site

                                                                                            Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

                                                                                            The site uses pro-étale objects obtained locally from inverse systems of étale objects with eventual finite étale transition maps, using the coverings of Scholze §3. This is distinct from the weakly étale scheme site.

                                                                                              • For any family to U there exists a smallest sieve containing the family.
                                                                                              • The smallest sieve containing the specified family is unique.

                                                                                              • The empty subpresheaf is the smallest sieve on U.
                                                                                              Sieve on an object

                                                                                              Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

                                                                                              A sieve on UU is a subpresheaf S⊆hUS\subseteq h_U of the representable presheaf. Equivalently its arrows with target UU are closed under precomposition. The pullback along V→UV\to U is S×hUhV⊆hVS\times_{h_U}h_V\subseteq h_V.

                                                                                                  Smooth topology

                                                                                                  Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi · Connections between diagrams

                                                                                                  Jointly surjective smooth families. Smooth surjections admit sections étale locally on the target, so their generated topology is already étale.

                                                                                                  Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.

                                                                                                  Local objects. For a separated Noetherian base S and an affine structural map P → S, the local lifting condition holds exactly for spectra of strictly henselian local rings (by equality with étale).

                                                                                                  Spectral

                                                                                                  Absolute · global

                                                                                                  Quasi-compact, sober, with a basis of quasi-compact opens stable under finite intersection. A scheme has spectral underlying space exactly when it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

                                                                                                  Properties of X itself. For separatedness, the base of the structure morphism is Spec⁡ℤ\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z.

                                                                                                  Spectral étale site

                                                                                                  Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

                                                                                                  Étaleness is characterized by étale π₀ and base change for the homotopy groups; covers are detected on ordinary spectra of π₀. Spectral here refers to ring spectra, a different usage from Hochster’s spectral spaces.

                                                                                                  Opposite category of connective E∞-rings, or relative version

                                                                                                  Lurie, Spectral Algebraic Geometry · G000068

                                                                                                    Spectral map

                                                                                                    Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

                                                                                                    Inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. The corresponding pullback on bounded distributive lattices preserves finite joins and meets.

                                                                                                        Valuative (v) topology

                                                                                                        Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

                                                                                                        For a map of qcqs schemes Y→XY\to X, test every Spec⁡V→X\operatorname{Spec}V\to X for a valuation ring VV. There must be an injective local map of valuation rings V↪WV\hookrightarrow W and a lift Spec⁡W→Y\operatorname{Spec}W\to Y over XX. For families, work affine locally on the target and take finite affine refinements whose disjoint union passes the test.

                                                                                                        The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.

                                                                                                        Weakly contractible object of a site

                                                                                                        Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

                                                                                                        An object UU is weakly contractible if evaluation at UU sends epimorphisms of sheaves of sets to surjections. Equivalently the canonical map ∐ihUi#→hU#\coprod_i h_{U_i}^\#\to h_U^\# in sheaves admits a section for every covering {Ui→U}\{U_i\to U\}.

                                                                                                        Zariski topology

                                                                                                        Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi · Connections between diagrams

                                                                                                        Jointly surjective open immersions. On the finite-type site one can take finite families, including the empty cover of the empty scheme.

                                                                                                        Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.

                                                                                                        Local objects. For a separated Noetherian base S and an affine structural map P → S, the local lifting condition holds exactly for spectra of local rings.

                                                                                                        On the relative prismatic category, use the completions of Zariski localizations of prism rings.                                                                                                         Appendix D, equivalent descriptions

                                                                                                        Universal homeomorphisms are integral, surjective and universally injective.                                                                                                         Fppf topology = Fpqc topology

                                                                                                        Equivalence · Fppf topology ⇔ Fpqc topology · Classical refinement

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.

                                                                                                        Grothendieck diagram

                                                                                                        Every fppf family is fpqc. For the converse in this finite-type category over a Noetherian base, every source is locally of finite type over the base, hence locally of finite type over its target. The target is locally Noetherian, so the morphism is locally of finite presentation. An fpqc covering family is flat and jointly surjective, hence fppf here.

                                                                                                        Stacks 022C · fppf covers are fpqc · Stacks 01T8 · local finite type over the target · Stacks 01T6 · local Noetherianity of schemes locally of finite type over the base · Stacks 01TX · local finite presentation over a locally Noetherian target · T000006

                                                                                                        Fpqc topology is coarser than Canonical topology

                                                                                                        Topology refinement · Fpqc topology · Classical refinement → Canonical topology

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.

                                                                                                        Grothendieck diagram

                                                                                                        Every representable restricts from a representable fpqc sheaf on the big site. The indicated full category is closed under fibre products over its objects, so the sheaf condition applies to its fpqc covering families and their overlaps. The canonical topology contains every such covering sieve.

                                                                                                        Fpqc topology is coarser than Valuative (v) topology

                                                                                                        Topology refinement · Fpqc topology · Valuative refinement → Valuative (v) topology

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.

                                                                                                        Grothendieck diagram

                                                                                                        After base change to Spec⁡V\operatorname{Spec}V, a faithfully flat cover lifts the specialization from the generic point to the closed point. A valuation-ring extension dominating that lifted specialization gives the required square. For general families use an affine-local standard fpqc refinement.

                                                                                                        Stacks 0ETA · valuation lifting and comparison with fpqc and ph · T000029

                                                                                                        Ph topology is coarser than Valuative (v) topology

                                                                                                        Topology refinement · Ph topology → Valuative (v) topology

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.

                                                                                                        Grothendieck diagram

                                                                                                        Given a proper surjection, choose a point over the generic point after base change to Spec⁡V\operatorname{Spec}V. Extend the valuation to the residue field of the chosen point and use the valuative criterion of properness. Zariski covers already satisfy the valuation test.

                                                                                                        Stacks 0ETA · valuation lifting and comparison with fpqc and ph · T000030

                                                                                                        Valuative (v) topology is coarser than Arc topology

                                                                                                        Topology refinement · Valuative (v) topology → Arc topology

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.

                                                                                                        Grothendieck diagram

                                                                                                        The valuation test can be expressed as lifting the specialization from the generic point to the closed point after base change to a valuation spectrum. Over a rank-one valuation ring, lifting that pair of points yields an extension of rank one. Thus an arbitrary-rank cover satisfies the rank-at-most-one test. See Proposition 2.1 and Corollary 2.5 of Bhatt–Mathew.

                                                                                                        Bhatt–Mathew, The arc-topology · Rydh, Submersions and effective descent of étale morphisms · T000031

                                                                                                        The forgetful functor (U,T,δ)↦U(U,T,\delta)\mapsto U is continuous and cocontinuous and preserves products and fibre products. The induced geometric morphism is uX/S:(X/S)cris→Sh⁡(XZar)u_{X/S}:(X/S)_{\mathrm{cris}}\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{Zar}}). For each open V⊆XV\subseteq X, (uX/S,∗ℱ)(V)=Γ((V/S)cris,ℱ∣(V/S)cris)(u_{X/S,*}\mathcal F)(V)=\Gamma((V/S)_{\mathrm{cris}},\mathcal F|_{(V/S)_{\mathrm{cris}}}).                                                                                                         Implication · Canonical Grothendieck topology ⇒ Subcanonical topology

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix a small category 𝒞\mathcal C and use its canonical topology JcanJ_{\mathrm{can}}.

                                                                                                        Grothendieck diagram

                                                                                                        Every representable presheaf on 𝒞\mathcal C is a JcanJ_{\mathrm{can}}-sheaf. Thus the canonical topology itself satisfies the predicate of subcanonicality.

                                                                                                        Stacks 00ZA · definition of the canonical topology · T000181

                                                                                                        Localize at ∞-connective morphisms

                                                                                                        Construction · ∞-topos → Hypercompletion

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Let 𝒳\mathcal X be an ∞-topos.

                                                                                                        Grothendieck diagram

                                                                                                        The ∞-connective maps are stable under pullback and form a strongly saturated class of small generation. Their localization is accessible and left exact; its target 𝒳∧\mathcal X^\wedge is again an ∞-topos.

                                                                                                        Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Proposition 6.5.2.8 and following construction · T000176

                                                                                                        Hypercompletion produces a hypercomplete ∞-topos

                                                                                                        Construction · Hypercompletion → Hypercomplete ∞-topos

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Let 𝒳\mathcal X be an ∞-topos.

                                                                                                        Grothendieck diagram

                                                                                                        The ∞-topos 𝒳∧\mathcal X^\wedge is hypercomplete. The original 𝒳\mathcal X is hypercomplete precisely when the localization functor is an equivalence.

                                                                                                        Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Lemma 6.5.2.12 · T000177

                                                                                                        Objects retained by hypercompletion

                                                                                                        Comparison under hypotheses · Hypercomplete object · Hypercompletion

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Let ZZ be an object of an ∞-topos 𝒳\mathcal X.

                                                                                                        Grothendieck diagram

                                                                                                        ZZ is hypercomplete if and only if it is in the essential image of 𝒳∧↪𝒳\mathcal X^\wedge\hookrightarrow\mathcal X; equivalently its localization unit is an equivalence.

                                                                                                        Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, §6.5.2 · T000178

                                                                                                        Criterion by effectivity in all slices

                                                                                                        Comparison under hypotheses · Hypercomplete ∞-topos · Effective hypercover

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Let 𝒳\mathcal X be an ∞-topos.

                                                                                                        Grothendieck diagram

                                                                                                        𝒳\mathcal X is hypercomplete if and only if, for every object VV of 𝒳\mathcal X, every hypercover of VV in the slice 𝒳/V\mathcal X_{/V} is effective.

                                                                                                        Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Theorem 6.5.3.12 · T000182

                                                                                                        An effective hypercover is a hypercover

                                                                                                        Implication · Effective hypercover ⇒ Hypercover

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Let 𝒳\mathcal X be an ∞-topos and let V∈𝒳V\in\mathcal X.

                                                                                                        Grothendieck diagram

                                                                                                        Effectivity adds the colimit condition to the degreewise effective epimorphism conditions.

                                                                                                        Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Definition 6.5.3.2 · T000183

                                                                                                        A bounded prism is a prism

                                                                                                        Implication · Bounded prism ⇒ Prism

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Work at a fixed prime p.

                                                                                                        Grothendieck diagram

                                                                                                        Boundedness is an extra uniform annihilation condition on the p-power torsion of the quotient; all prism axioms remain required.

                                                                                                        Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Definition 1.1 · T000179

                                                                                                        Pass to the opposite category

                                                                                                        Construction · Frame → Locale

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Take the category of frames with homomorphisms preserving finite meets and arbitrary joins.

                                                                                                        Grothendieck diagram

                                                                                                        The category Loc\mathrm{Loc} is Frmop\mathrm{Frm}^{\mathrm{op}}. The object assignment is unchanged and each morphism is reversed.

                                                                                                        Banaschewski, Radical ideals and coherent frames, §1 · T000180

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        This singleton is a generator of the prime-to-ℓ finite flat topology.

                                                                                                        Gabber–Kelly, Points in algebraic geometry, Definition 2.5(5)

                                                                                                        Proper covering family

                                                                                                        covering family · Proper → Proper topology

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Work over a separated Noetherian base S, in the category of separated schemes of finite type over S. Take a finite family with common target T. Each arrow is proper and the images jointly cover T.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        This family is one of the generators of the proper topology and therefore also covers for the h topology.

                                                                                                        Gabber–Kelly, Points in algebraic geometry, Definition 2.5(10), (17)

                                                                                                        Completely decomposed proper family

                                                                                                        covering family · Proper → Envelope topology

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Work over a separated Noetherian base S, in the category of separated schemes of finite type over S. Take a finite family with common target T. Every arrow is proper. For each point t of T, some source contains a point above t inducing an isomorphism on residue fields.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        This family is a generator of the envelope topology.

                                                                                                        Gabber–Kelly, Points in algebraic geometry, Definition 2.5(8)

                                                                                                        An open immersion as an object

                                                                                                        site objects · Open immersion → Petit Zariski site

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix a scheme S and a size-bounded big site of schemes containing S. Use the slice category of schemes over S.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        An open immersion U → S is an object of the small Zariski site. A family of open immersions over U covers when the images cover U.

                                                                                                        Stacks 020T · the big Zariski slice and its small open subsite · Stacks 020O · open immersions in a Zariski covering

                                                                                                        An étale morphism as an object

                                                                                                        site objects · Étale → Petit étale site

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix a scheme S and a size-bounded big site of schemes containing S. Use the slice category of schemes over S.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        An étale morphism U → S is an object of the small étale site. Covering such an object requires a jointly surjective étale family over U.

                                                                                                        Stacks 021B · the big étale slice and its small étale subsite · Stacks 0215 · étale covering families

                                                                                                        Full subsite of open S-schemes

                                                                                                        site presentation · Petit Zariski site → Gros Zariski site

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix a scheme S and a size-bounded big site of schemes containing S. Use the slice category of schemes over S.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        The full subcategory on open immersions into S, with the induced Zariski coverings, presents the small Zariski site. In the big site arbitrary S-schemes may be objects.

                                                                                                        Stacks 020T · the big Zariski slice and its small open subsite

                                                                                                        Full subsite of étale S-schemes

                                                                                                        site presentation · Petit étale site → Gros étale site

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix a scheme S and a size-bounded big site of schemes containing S. Use the slice category of schemes over S.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        The full subcategory on étale S-schemes, with the induced étale coverings, is the small étale site. The inclusion describes the object classes and covering families.

                                                                                                        Stacks 021B · the big étale slice and its small étale subsite

                                                                                                        Big Zariski site

                                                                                                        site presentation · Zariski topology → Gros Zariski site

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix a scheme S and a size-bounded big site of schemes containing S. Use the slice category of schemes over S.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        Every object of this slice is an S-scheme. The covering arrows over any object T are jointly surjective families of open immersions. The classical topology diagram restricts this family criterion to its stated finite-type category.

                                                                                                        Stacks 020T · the big Zariski slice and its small open subsite · Stacks 020O · open immersions in a Zariski covering

                                                                                                        Big étale site

                                                                                                        site presentation · Étale topology → Gros étale site

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix a scheme S and a size-bounded big site of schemes containing S. Use the slice category of schemes over S.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        Every object of this slice is an S-scheme. The covering arrows over any object T are jointly surjective families of étale morphisms. The classical topology diagram restricts this family criterion to its stated finite-type category.

                                                                                                        Stacks 021B · the big étale slice and its small étale subsite · Stacks 0215 · étale covering families

                                                                                                        Big fppf site

                                                                                                        site presentation · Fppf topology → Big fppf site

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix a scheme S and a size-bounded big site of schemes containing S. Use the slice category of schemes over S.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        Every object of this slice is an S-scheme. The covering arrows over any object T are jointly surjective families of flat morphisms locally of finite presentation. The classical topology diagram restricts this family criterion to its stated finite-type category.

                                                                                                        Descent of maps into schemes

                                                                                                        descent · Fpqc topology · Classical refinement → Subcanonical topology

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix a scheme Z. For each test scheme T, take the presheaf value Hom(T, Z). Use fpqc coverings of schemes.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        Compatible arrows into Z on an fpqc cover descend to a unique arrow T → Z. In particular, the representable presheaves are sheaves.

                                                                                                        Stacks 03O3 · representable functors satisfy fpqc descent

                                                                                                        Topological invariance of the étale site

                                                                                                        invariance · Universal homeomorphism → Petit étale site

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Let f : X → Y be a universal homeomorphism of schemes. Use compatible choices for the two small étale sites.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        Base change along f gives an equivalence of the categories of étale schemes over Y and X; it preserves and reflects étale covering families and induces an equivalence of their small étale topoi.

                                                                                                        Stacks 04DZ · base change of étale schemes under a universal homeomorphism · Stacks 03SI · invariance of small étale sites and topoi

                                                                                                        Affineness over an affine base

                                                                                                        structure morphism · Affine · scheme → Affine · morphism

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix the structure morphism p : X → S of a scheme over an affine base S.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        The scheme X is affine if and only if p is affine. The affine base gives a one-chart test for affineness of the morphism.

                                                                                                        Stacks 01S8 · affineness tested on an affine covering of the target · Hoyois §1.5, opening diagram of classes of schemes · Hoyois §8.1, opening diagram of local/global and relative/absolute properties

                                                                                                        Quasi-compactness over an affine base

                                                                                                        structure morphism · Quasi-compact · scheme → Quasi-compact · morphism

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix the structure morphism p : X → S over an affine scheme S.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        The scheme X is quasi-compact if and only if p is quasi-compact. The inverse image of the single affine chart S is X.

                                                                                                        Stacks 01K4 · affine-open test for a quasi-compact morphism · Hoyois §8.1, opening diagram of local/global and relative/absolute properties

                                                                                                        Quasi-separatedness over an affine base

                                                                                                        structure morphism · Quasi-separated · scheme → Quasi-separated · morphism

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix the structure morphism p : X → S over an affine scheme S.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        The morphism p is quasi-separated if and only if intersections of pairs of affine opens of X are quasi-compact, which characterizes quasi-separated X.

                                                                                                        Stacks 01KO · relative affine intersection criterion · Hoyois §8.1, opening diagram of local/global and relative/absolute properties

                                                                                                        Absolute separation via the structure morphism

                                                                                                        structure morphism · Separated · scheme → Separated · morphism

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. For a scheme X use its canonical structure morphism to the spectrum of the integers.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        Separatedness of X means that this specific morphism is separated. The test is whether its relative diagonal is a closed immersion.

                                                                                                        Stacks 01KK · separated morphisms and separated schemes · Hoyois §8.1, opening diagram of local/global and relative/absolute properties

                                                                                                        Quasi-compact opens as a basis

                                                                                                        basis comparison · Qcqs scheme → Qc Zariski basis site

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Give its quasi-compact opens the induced Zariski coverings.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        Affine opens form a basis. Quasi-compact opens are closed under finite intersection, and coverings of such an open have finite subcovers. Restriction to this basis gives the same sheaves as on all opens.

                                                                                                        Stacks 01KO · quasi-compact intersections · Stacks 009H · comparison of sheaves on a basis

                                                                                                        Open immersion to its open subscheme

                                                                                                        classification · Open immersion → Open subschemes of X

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix a target scheme X. Identify two open immersions into X when their sources are isomorphic over X.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        An immersion in this class identifies its source with its open image U equipped with the restriction of the structure sheaf of X. Factorization over X corresponds to inclusion of open subschemes.

                                                                                                        Stacks 01IO · open immersions and open subschemes · Stacks 01HG · the structure sheaf on an open subspace · Hoyois §8.2, classification diagram following Corollary 8.19

                                                                                                        Closed immersion to its closed subscheme

                                                                                                        classification · Closed immersion → Closed subschemes of X, opposite order

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Fix a target scheme X. Identify closed immersions up to isomorphism of their sources over X. The diagram uses the opposite of the usual inclusion order on closed subschemes.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        A closed immersion i determines a closed subscheme with defining ideal ker(𝒪_X → i_*𝒪_Z). Factorization of one closed immersion through another reverses inclusion of their defining ideals. Passing to the opposite order makes the ideal correspondence order preserving.

                                                                                                        Stacks 01IO · closed immersions and closed subschemes · Stacks 01QO · the quotient-ring description and the quasi-coherent kernel · Hoyois §8.2, classification diagram following Corollary 8.19

                                                                                                        A projective compactification gives a relatively ample line bundle

                                                                                                        Implication · Quasi-projective in the open-in-projective sense ⇒ Quasi-projective

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. Let X → S factor through a quasi-compact open immersion into a projective S-scheme.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        The projective scheme has a relatively ample invertible sheaf. Its restriction to X remains relatively ample, as seen over each affine open of S. The quasi-compact open immersion and the projective morphism are of finite type.

                                                                                                        Marc Hoyois, Algebraic Geometry, Definition 4.35(ii), the open-in-projective convention · Stacks 07RL · projective implies quasi-projective · Stacks 0B3E · restriction of ampleness along a quasi-compact immersion · Stacks 01VW · finite type with a relatively ample invertible sheaf · Hoyois, Chapter 8, relative/global panel

                                                                                                        Projective compactification over a qcqs base

                                                                                                        Comparison under hypotheses · Quasi-projective ∧ Qcqs target → Quasi-projective in the open-in-projective sense

                                                                                                        Hypotheses. The target S is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The morphism X → S is of finite type with a relatively ample invertible sheaf.

                                                                                                        Comparison across diagrams

                                                                                                        The morphism factors through an open immersion into a projective S-scheme. This open immersion is quasi-compact because X → S is quasi-compact and the projective S-scheme is separated.

                                                                                                        Stacks 07RM · projective compactification over a qcqs base · Marc Hoyois, Algebraic Geometry, Definition 4.35(ii), the open-in-projective convention · Hoyois, Chapter 8, relative/global panel

                                                                                                        Universal homeomorphism
                                                                                                        Definition
                                                                                                        Every base change is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces. No isomorphism of structure sheaves is required.
                                                                                                        Setting
                                                                                                        A universal property holds on the underlying spaces after every scheme base change Y′→YY^{\prime}\to Y.
